transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in?

Hi, doctor. Thank you for having me. I, um... I hope I'm explaining this right, so just let me know if I'm not. But I guess what brought me in is... I just don't really feel like myself anymore. 

It's probably nothing too terrible, I don't want to sound like I'm just complaining, but I've just been going really flat and quiet lately. I barely talk to people. And at work—I'm a building cleaner—even just getting started on my cleaning route, it feels like... well, like pushing a loaded cart uphill. I know everyone gets tired, but it just takes so much out of me right now. Is that... does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
How long have you been feeling this way—weeks, months, or longer?

Well, um... I guess it's been a little while now. I hope I'm not making a bigger deal out of it than I should. But it's been building for about... oh, a year and five months? Give or take a little. 

It seemed to start right around the time I had to leave my old apartment and, you know, move away from my old neighborhood. I know moving is just a normal part of life and I should probably be over it by now, so I'm sorry if I'm just being overly sensitive about it. I hope it's okay that I brought that up. Does that give you the timeline you need?

Since this started about a year and five months ago, have you been feeling this low and tired pretty much every day without much let-up, or does it come and go—like some weeks feeling better and other weeks much worse?

Well, um... I guess it's been pretty steady. I mean, I don't want to sound like I'm whining, because I know everyone has bad days, but... yeah, it feels like it's just been kind of a constant low. 

There aren't really weeks where I suddenly feel great and energetic. It's just sort of this... this heavy feeling most days. I try to push through it, I really do, and I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is. I just... I don't really get those breaks where the tiredness lifts. Is that... is that the kind of detail you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions right.

Over this past year and five months, has there been any stretch of at least two weeks where your mood, energy, or interest dropped even further below this baseline you've described, or has it stayed pretty much the same level the whole time?

Well, um... I guess if I really think about it, there was a point where it got a bit harder. I hope I'm not confusing things, but... the really low part, where it felt like I just couldn't shake it at all, that's been going on for about a year and two months now. 

It started maybe a few months after I moved. I tried to just keep my chin up, you know? I didn't want to be a burden to anyone or complain too much, so I just kept going to work and doing my best. But yeah, that heavier feeling... it's been pretty constant for about a year and two months. I'm sorry if that's a bit different from what I said a minute ago, I just want to make sure I'm giving you the most accurate timeline. Is that helpful?

During that more intense period over the last year or so, have you also noticed changes like losing interest in things you used to enjoy, trouble sleeping or sleeping too much, changes in appetite, or difficulty concentrating?

Well, um... I guess I have noticed a little change with some of the things I usually like to do. I hope it doesn't sound like I'm just being lazy, because I really try to stay active. But... well, I used to really look forward to going fishing on Saturdays, or just sitting down with my coffee and a crossword puzzle. And at work—I'm a janitor—I used to get a kick out of showing the younger guys some tricks for stripping a floor, you know, passing on what I know. 

But lately... I don't know, I just kind of let those things sit. It's not that I don't want to be helpful or do things, it's just that they don't seem to give me anything back right now. I just don't get that same spark from them. I'm sorry, I hope I'm explaining that right. Is that the kind of thing you mean? I don't want to make it sound like I've just given up on everything, because I haven't.
During that more intense period over the last year or so, have you noticed any changes in your sleep—like trouble falling or staying asleep, or sleeping much more than usual?

Well, um... my sleep? I guess it's been okay, mostly. I mean, I don't want to make a big fuss about it. I know getting older means you don't sleep like a teenager anymore, right? 

I... I haven't really noticed anything too out of the ordinary. Maybe a night here or there where it takes a minute to wind down, but nothing I'd call real trouble. I try to make sure I get enough rest so I can do a good job at work the next day. I hope that's the kind of answer you're looking for? I just don't think there's much to report on the sleep front, if that's alright.

During that more intense period over the last year or so, have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight—eating noticeably more or less than usual, or gaining or losing weight without trying?

Well, um... I guess... I mean, I don't want to complain, because I know there are folks out there who don't have enough to eat, right? But... I have noticed I'm just not as hungry lately. 

It's silly, really, but most days food just kind of... tastes like cardboard to me. So I might skip a meal here and there, or just have a few crackers when I get home after my shift, just to put something in my stomach. I try to make sure I'm still eating, I promise. But... well, I guess my work pants have been hanging a bit looser than they used to. I just tighten my belt an extra notch so I don't look unkempt at work. I hope it's not a big deal, I just... I haven't had much of an appetite. Is that the sort of thing you needed to know?
During that more intense year or so, have you noticed any trouble concentrating or making decisions—like losing your train of thought at work or having a harder time focusing on tasks?

Well, um... no, I don't think I've had much trouble with that. I mean, I really try to stay on top of things, especially at work. If you don't pay attention when you're cleaning, you miss spots, right? And I'd hate to let anyone down or have my supervisor think I wasn't pulling my weight. 

I guess... maybe if I'm just a little tired, I might have to double-check my supply cart to make sure I grabbed enough paper towels for the bathrooms, but nothing serious. My mind still feels pretty clear, and I can focus just fine when I need to. I hope that's a good sign? I just haven't really noticed any big problems with my concentration, if that's okay.
During this more intense past year or so, have you had any thoughts about death, dying, or that you'd be better off not being around?

Well, um... I really don't want you to think I'm crazy or... or ungrateful for the life I have. I know I should just put my head down and be thankful I can still work. But... well, I guess I have had some thoughts like that. 

I don't have some big plan or anything, I promise. I would never want to do something that would cause a mess for somebody else to clean up. But... a lot of mornings lately, I wake up and just kind of think... maybe it would be easier if I just didn't wake up at all. 

It actually scares me a bit, which is why I'm even saying it out loud to you. I usually try to keep that sort of thing to myself so I don't bother anyone. I hope you're not disappointed in me for thinking that way. Is it okay that I told you that?

Before this all started about a year and five months ago, had you ever gone through a similar stretch of feeling low, tired, or flat—even mildly—for months or years, or is this the first time in your life you've felt this way?

Well, um... no, I don't think so. I mean, I've always tried to just keep a positive attitude, you know? I've been working steadily for a long time, and I usually just... just do my job and try to be pleasant to the people in the building. 

I don't remember ever feeling quite this... heavy before. I mean, everyone has a bad day here and there, right? But nothing that lasted like this, or made it so hard to just get out of bed. I've always been pretty reliable before this last year or so. I hope that makes sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.

Over this past year or so, has this low mood and lack of energy made it hard for you to keep up with your work duties or daily responsibilities—like struggling to complete your cleaning route or take care of things at home—or have you generally still been able to manage, even if it's harder than before?

Well, um... I really try my hardest to push through, I promise. I don't like to make excuses or be a bother to anyone. But... well, to be honest, it has gotten pretty hard lately. I'm actually a little ashamed to admit this, but... my supervisor actually started writing me up. I was missing some of my routes and making repeated cleaning mistakes. I felt just awful about it, I really hate letting my team down.

And, um... outside of work, I guess I've let things slide, too. I just stopped keeping up with church, and I haven't been fishing at all... I even stopped checking in on the people I usually visit. I just haven't had the energy to do any of it. 

It finally got to the point where I couldn't even keep my work routine straight anymore, which is so embarrassing for me. So... I finally went to the employee assistance program for help. I didn't want to lose my job or cause extra work for anyone else to clean up after me. I hope going to them was the right thing to do? I just really want to get back to being reliable again, if that makes sense.

I don't remember ever feeling quite this... heavy before. I mean, everyone has a bad day here and there, right? But nothing that lasted like this, or made it so hard to just get out of bed. I've always been pretty reliable before this last year or so. I hope that makes sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.

inference.note: No prior history of chronic low mood before this episode, and the total duration (~17 months) is under the 2-year threshold required for dysthymia (F34.1), so this is ruled out. The presence of anhedonia, appetite/weight loss, and passive suicidal ideation during the intensified period suggests a single major depressive episode of at least moderate, possibly severe, intensity (F32.1/F32.2) rather than a chronic dysthymic pattern.

doctor.intent: Assess overall functional impairment to distinguish moderate from severe depression—specifically whether he is still able to carry out his daily work and responsibilities or if it has become very difficult to function at all
doctor.question: Over this past year or so, has this low mood and lack of energy made it hard for you to keep up with your work duties or daily responsibilities—like struggling to complete your cleaning route or take care of things at home—or have you generally still been able to manage, even if it's harder than before?

target_item.name: Functional Impairment
target_item.manifestation: My supervisor started writing up missed routes and repeated cleaning mistakes, and I stopped keeping up with church, fishing, and the people I used to check in on. I finally went to the employee assistance program because I could not keep my work routine straight anymore.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the impact of the symptoms on my daily life and work responsibilities, which corresponds to functional impairment.

patient.answer:
Well, um... I really try my hardest to push through, I promise. I don't like to make excuses or be a bother to anyone. But... well, to be honest, it has gotten pretty hard lately. I'm actually a little ashamed to admit this, but... my supervisor actually started writing me up. I was missing some of my routes and making repeated cleaning mistakes. I felt just awful about it, I really hate letting my team down.

And, um... outside of work, I guess I've let things slide, too. I just stopped keeping up with church, and I haven't been fishing at all... I even stopped checking in on the people I usually visit. I just haven't had the energy to do any of it. 

It finally got to the point where I couldn't even keep my work routine straight anymore, which is so embarrassing for me. So... I finally went to the employee assistance program for help. I didn't want to lose my job or cause extra work for anyone else to clean up after me. I hope going to them was the right thing to do? I just really want to get back to being reliable again, if that makes sense.

inference.note: Functional impairment (write-ups at work, missed routines), anhedonia, significant appetite/weight loss, and passive suicidal ideation without prior depressive history support a single severe depressive episode without psychotic features, ruling out F32.1 (moderate).

opening_question.intent: Identify the primary reason for the visit today
opening_question.question: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in?

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports a single, first-lifetime depressive episode lasting over a year, with clear depressed mood, anhedonia, appetite/weight loss, passive suicidal ideation, and significant functional impairment (disciplinary write-ups at work, withdrawal from social/religious activities). Symptoms meet criteria for a major depressive episode of severe intensity without psychotic features, distinguishing it from persistent depressive disorder (which lacks this degree of impairment and acute symptom burden) and from moderate MDD (given the severity of functional disruption and suicidal ideation).
